usageNotes: Use this to audit TFA enrollment across all users in the cluster — useful for compliance checks or onboarding reviews. Unprivileged users only receive their own entry; the full list requires Sys.Audit or equivalent realm-admin privilege. The response also surfaces lockout state (tfa-locked-until, totp-locked), making it useful for diagnosing why a user cannot complete login.

examples.summary: List all TFA configurations as an admin token

tips: An empty 'entries' array for a user means they have no TFA methods registered — not that TFA is disabled globally.
Check 'tfa-locked-until' (unix timestamp) and 'totp-locked' on a user's record before resetting credentials; a lockout may clear on its own.
TFA type 'recovery' indicates one-time recovery codes; if this is the only entry for a user, they have no active second factor.
u2f is legacy — users with only u2f entries should migrate to webauthn.
